dataset.title: Electricity import exposure: net electricity imports + power from imported fossil fuel, % of supply (derived)

indicator.name: Electricity import exposure
indicator.description: Share of a country's electricity supply that depends on imports: 100 × [max(N, 0) + Σ over coal, gas, oil of g_f × clamp(d_f, 0, 1)] ÷ (G + max(N, 0)). G = generation, N = net electricity imports, g_f = generation from fuel f (all TWh, Ember via OWID), d_f = the fuel's national net import dependence ((supply − production) ÷ supply, EI via OWID). Same country and year for every input.

notes: Computed by npm run data:import from 9 input datasets (src/lib/derive.ts, op "electricity-exposure"). For each entity, the latest year in which generation, net imports and coal/gas/oil generation all exist, and the dependence of every fuel with generation above 0 exists.

An exact value more than 2 years older than the latest year with generation and trade data is not used (maxLagYears = 2): e.g. a country whose fuel data stop in 2002 would otherwise be scored on 2002. Its bounds for the latest year are shown instead.
A fuel with zero generation adds exactly 0, so its dependence is not needed (e.g. Lesotho imports all its power and burns no fuel: 100 %).

Where a fuel is burned but its dependence is unknown (EI does not list most small countries), no value is given; the detail panel shows the bounds instead (unknown dependence taken as 0 % and as 100 %).
caveats: Assumes power plants import the same share of each fuel as the economy as a whole (economy-wide net import dependence). A country could, for example, burn domestic coal in power plants and import coal for steel.

Nuclear fuel is not counted: uranium is mostly imported (Japan, France, South Korea…), but no open dataset here gives uranium supply by country, so nuclear power counts as not import-exposed. Countries with large nuclear fleets are understated.
Net figures: transit trade, re-exports and stock changes are netted out. Imported electricity is counted as fully import-exposed; exported electricity is assumed to have the same mix as generation.
Covers electricity only (not transport fuel or heating), so it is a partial measure of energy dependence.

scoring.rationale: Scored by default as the Fuel & energy indicator: a literal 0–100 share, and unlike direct electricity trade it counts imported fuel burned at home (Japan ≈ 68 % instead of 0 %). Electricity only, so it does not cover transport fuel. To turn it off, set scoring.include to false in data/sources/electricity-import-exposure.derived.json (then npm run data:import), or set the Fuel & energy weight to 0 in the app.
